newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Crisis looms as Bangladesh replaces port chief.
newsitem.headline: Crisis looms as Bangladesh replaces port chief.

text.p: Bangladesh's main Chittagong port faced a new crisis on Thursday after the government suddenly replaced the port authority chairman and gave his job temporarily to a shipping executive, port officials said.

They said captain Zahiruddin Mahood, the former chairman of Chittagong Port Authority (CPA), was demoted as Member Operation (of the port) while Zulfikar Haider, managing director of Bangladesh Shipping Corporation (BSC), had taken charge as his interim successor.
A shipping ministry order issued on Wednesday also removed the CPA's director of traffic M. Mohsin Sarker. He was replaced by Sanoar Hossain, deputy director of traffic.

The changes followed a recent directive issued by the former CPA executives allowing port users to bring in private equipment to speed up handling of cargo, an issue that drew strong protests from port workers' unions.
The unions threatened to go on an indefinite strike unless the decision, taken at a meeting earlier this month at the office of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, was reversed.

The Shipping Ministry was apparently annoyed because the decision was conveyed by the CPA directly to the port users, including the Q.C. Shipping company which spearheaded the demand to use private equipment, bypassing the ministry, port officials said.
"The ministry got so angry that it immediately ordered the removal of the chairman and his lieutenant Sarkar," said one official who declined to be named.

"The decision to invite the relevant parties to use private equipment was taken in accordance with the decision of the meeting held at the prime minister's office on June 14," Mahmood said on Thursday.
"We pressed the CPA to issue the directive (following the decision) because the ministry seemed to be delaying it," said Amirul Haq, director of private Classic Corporation.
The Mayor of Chittagong, A.B.M. Mohiuddin Chowdhury, a senior figure in the ruling Awami League, also had a hand in having the CPA issue the directive, he said without giving details.

Chittagong port, which handles 80 percent of the country's exports and imports, have faced repeated work disruptions over the past few months as rival trade unions fought over the use of private equipment.
